h: Knitted jockeys and North Devon days out
p: The sheep racing is what everyone talks about, and with good reason. The woolly racers set off with little knitted jockeys on their backs, and the whole crowd picks a favourite to cheer on. It's daft, it's charming and the kids will be re-enacting it for days. Other shows around the park show off working dogs and farm skills, and they're a great way to learn a bit about country life without it feeling like a lesson.

The park sits just outside Bideford near Abbotsham, off the A39, so it's an easy one to reach by car if you're staying anywhere along the North Devon coast. Allow most of a day. Between the shows, the animals and the indoor play, families tend to stay longer than they expect.

Bring wellies or old trainers, because it's a working farm setting and the outside areas can get muddy after rain. A spare set of clothes for little ones is always a good idea at somewhere with this much to climb on and play in.

There's lots more to fill a holiday nearby. The Tarka Trail runs through Bideford and is a brilliant flat cycle and walking route along the estuary. Appledore, across the water, is a pretty fishing village of colourful cottages and narrow lanes. Westward Ho! has a big sandy beach and a famous pebble ridge, and Clovelly is a short drive west along the coast.
Feeling adventurous? Boat trips to Lundy Island sail from Bideford in season.
